extracted.intended_audience: graduate or advanced undergraduate students studying commutative algebra / algebraic geometry (readers of the referenced textbook and its exercise solutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of definitional equivalences, characterizations, and standard criteria appearing in textbook exercises and solutions from chapters on valuation rings, Jacobson rings, Noetherian/Artinian properties, primary decomposition, and related spectral/topological statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobson ring — algebraic criterion (Exercise 5.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: A is a Jacobson ring ⇔ every finitely generated A-algebra B which is a field is finite over A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: reduce to A ⊂ B, use Exercise 21 to find s ∈ A and a maximal ideal m not containing s, extend A→A/m to homomorphism g:B→(alg. closure of k); injectivity of g and algebraicity over k give finiteness. Note: book has typo 'the algebraic closure of k' vs 'an algebraic closure of k'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally closed subset — topological characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: A subset of X is locally closed iff it is the intersection of an open set and a closed set, equivalently iff it is open in its closure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short proof: if U open and C closed then U∩C is open in its closure and conversely; small set-theoretic inclusion checks suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Very dense subset — equivalent conditions (Part 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For X0 ⊂ X the following are equivalent: (1) every non-empty locally closed subset of X meets X0; (2) for every closed C in X we have X0 ∩ C = C; (3) the map U ↦ X0 ∩ U from open sets of X onto opens of X0 is bijective. Such X0 is 'very dense' in X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalences use complements and bijection/onjectivity arguments; see (3') and (3") reformulations in terms of closed sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobson ring — geometric characterizations (Part 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring A the following are equivalent: (i) A is Jacobson; (ii) the set M of maximal ideals is very dense in Spec(A); (iii) every locally closed subset of Spec(A) consisting of a single point is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to showing algebraic conditions on intersections of maximal ideals correspond to the topological conditions; uses Exercise 23 criteria and arguments about primes as intersections of larger primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal domination characterizes valuation rings (Exercise 5.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let K be a field and Σ the poset of local subrings of K ordered by domination. Σ has maximal elements; A ∈ Σ is maximal ⇔ A is a valuation ring of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embedding into algebraic closure of residue field and the poset Φ(K,Ω) machinery; Lemma references show any maximal dominating local ring must be valuation ring and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation ring ⇔ ideals totally ordered (Exercise 5.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an integral domain A with fraction field K: A is a valuation ring of K ⇔ for any two ideals a,b of A, either a ⊂ b or b ⊂ a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalence proved by reducing to existence of incomparable principal ideals; deductions: if A is a valuation ring then Ap and A/p are valuation rings of their fraction fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrings containing a valuation ring are localizations (Exercise 5.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a valuation ring of K then every subring B of K containing A is a localization of A at a prime: B = Ap for some prime p ⊂ A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: B is local; set p = A∩ maximal_ideal(B) and check B = Ap by showing any b∈B ackslash A has inverse in A that is a unit in B and so b∈Ap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value group and ultrametric inequality (Exercise 5.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given valuation ring A⊂K with unit group U, Γ = K*/U; ordering ξ≥η defined via representatives x,y by xy^{-1}∈A; Γ is a totally ordered abelian group and the canonical map v:K*→Γ satisfies v(x+y) ≥ min(v(x),v(y)) whenever x+y≠0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To check inequality assume v(x)≥v(y) so xy^{-1}∈A and deduce (x+y)y^{-1}∈A; standard valuation group construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation ⇔ valuation ring equivalence (Exercise 5.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: A valuation v:K*→Γ (Γ totally ordered abelian group) satisfies (1) v(xy)=v(x)+v(y) and (2) v(x+y) ≥ min(v(x),v(y)) (or x+y=0). Then {x∈K : v(x)≥0} ∪ {0} is a valuation ring of K; conversely any valuation ring arises this way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus valuations and valuation rings are essentially equivalent concepts; extend v uniquely from group algebra to fraction field in constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectra of products of valuation domains with matching value sets are homeomorphic (Proposition 76)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given families of valuation domains Aj and Bj with same value-image of certain ideals (vj(aj)=wj(bj)), form A=∏ Aj/aj and B=∏ Bj/bj; then Spec(A) and Spec(B) are homeomorphic. The proof supplies an explicit description of spectra in terms of monoids Mj, product M and a poset P of upward closed sets satisfying stability under ∧ and additivity condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The valuation maps induce a lattice isomorphism from ideals of A to certain upward-closed subsets I ⊂ M; primes correspond to P ⊂ I. Reader is left to verify details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primes ↔ isolated subgroups of value group; value groups of Ap and A/p (Exercise 5.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For valuation ring A with value group Γ, the map p ↦ v(A ackslash p) identifies Spec(A) bijectively with isolated subgroups ∆ ⊂ Γ (∆ isolated means 0≤β≤α and α∈∆ ⇒ β∈∆). (b) Γ(Ap) ≅ Γ/∆ and Γ(A/p) ≅ ∆ as ordered groups/monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: S=A ackslash p generates subgroup S/A* whose image ∆ is isolated; converses given by p=A ackslash v^{-1}(∆+ )∪{0}. Proof includes explicit isomorphisms (45),(46),(47).

rubrics_metrics.name: Realizing a given ordered abelian group as value group (Exercise 5.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given totally ordered abelian group Γ and a field k, form group algebra A=k[Γ] with basis x_α (α∈Γ); A is domain. Define v0 on nonzero u=∑λ_i x_{α_i} by v0(u)=α_1 (smallest exponent). v0 satisfies valuation axioms and extends uniquely to valuation v on fraction field K with value group Γ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction is explicit: order monomials by Γ and take leading term; extension to fraction field standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closedness of Spec after base-change characterizes integrality (Exercise 5.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f:A→B is integral then for any A-algebra C the map (f⊗1)^*:Spec(B⊗_A C)→Spec(C) is closed. Conversely, if (f⊗1)^* is closed for all C and B is a domain (or has finitely many minimal primes), then f is integral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of converse: reduce to A⊂B domain, take valuation ring A' of fraction field of B containing A; closedness of Spec(B⊗_A A')→Spec(A') and Exercise 5.35 imply BA'=A'. Thus B⊂A' so B integral over A. For finitely many minimal primes, reduce to B/N and lift integrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jordan–Hölder invariance for modules (Section 7.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite-length A-module M, any two composition series have the same multiset of isomorphism classes of composition factors (i.e., χ(α)=χ(β) for any two composition series α,β).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on length using intersection arguments of successive terms; standard Jordan–Hölder argument adapted from group case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endomorphism rigidity for Noetherian / Artinian modules (Exercise 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) If M is Noetherian and u:M→M is surjective then u is an isomorphism. (ii) If M is Artinian and u injective then u is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) follows since Noetherian ⇒ finitely generated and surjective endomorphism of finitely generated module is bijective (use Nakayama-type or module finiteness arguments). For (ii) dualize to images or use descending chains of Im(u^n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: Noetherian module via finitely generated submodules maximality (Exercise 6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module M is Noetherian iff every non-empty set of finitely generated submodules of M has a maximal element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition that M Noetherian ⇔ every submodule finitely generated to reduce to Zorn-type arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability of Noetherian/Artinian under intersection/quotients (Exercise 6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M/N1 and M/N2 are Noetherian then M/(N1∩N2) is Noetherian; similarly replacing 'Noetherian' by 'Artinian'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact sequences 0→N1/(N1∩N2)→M/(N1∩N2)→M/N1→0 and analogous ones; finite generalization for intersections of finitely many Ni holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annihilator quotient of Noetherian module is Noetherian ring (Exercise 6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a Noetherian A-module and a = Ann_A(M), then A/a is a Noetherian ring. (Replacing 'Noetherian' by 'Artinian' is not generally true.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that M finitely generated implies certain quotient rings inherit noetherianity; reference to book exercise for (b) counterexample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian space definitions and consequences (Exercises 6.5–6.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A topological space X is Noetherian iff opens satisfy ACC (equivalently closed subsets satisfy DCC). Consequences: every subspace is Noetherian; X is quasi-compact; equivalently every open subspace is quasi-compact; a Noetherian space is a finite union of irreducible closed subspaces and thus has finitely many irreducible components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use maximal/minimal conditions and standard finite-union/cover arguments; see exercise hints using maximal elements of families of closed sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian rings and their spectra (Exercises 6.8–6.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian then Spec(A) is a Noetherian topological space. The converse is false in general. In a Noetherian ring the set of minimal prime ideals is finite and the set of primes satisfies ACC. Also, for a Noetherian module M, Supp(M) is a closed Noetherian subspace of Spec(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counterexample to converse: A = K^N (K-valued functions on N) is absolutely flat with maximal primes but has ascending chains of radical ideals; use V(a) chain ↔ ideal chain correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closedness of f* equivalent to going-up when Spec(B) Noetherian (Exercise 6.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f:A→B with Spec(B) Noetherian, then f* : Spec(B)→Spec(A) is closed ⇔ f has the going-up property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One direction is standard in the book; conversely use decomposition of V(b) into minimal primes and apply going-up to those minimal primes to check images of closed sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert Basis Theorem (Theorem 78)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a Noetherian ring then A[t] is Noetherian; more generally if M is Noetherian A-module then M[t] is a Noetherian A[t]-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses degree minimization of an infinite increasing chain of submodules and leading-coefficient generation arguments; construct relation producing contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma correction: irreducible ideals and primary ideals (Lemma 7.12 remark)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Noetherian ring every proper irreducible ideal is primary (the book missed 'proper'). Also primary ideals in Noetherian rings can be reducible: example (x^2,xy,y^2) is (x,y)-primary but reducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof correction shows equalities Ann(x^n)=Ann(x^{n+1}) lead to (x^n)∩(y)=(0) enabling primary argument; includes related equivalence for Krull dimension ≤0: (a) dim≤0 ⇔ (b) A/N absolutely flat ⇔ (c) (a)⊃(a^2)⊃... stabilizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary decomposition existence and topology of Spec(A) (Theorem 7.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Noetherian ring every ideal has a primary decomposition. Consequently, closed subsets of Spec(A) are finite unions of V(p) with p prime; equivalently closed sets are closures of finite subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses finiteness of minimal primes over ideals in Noetherian rings; description implies poset-structure determines Zariski topology in Noetherian case.

rubrics_metrics.name: I. S. Cohen criterion for Noetherianness (Exercise 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is non-Noetherian let Σ be ideals not finitely generated; Σ has maximal elements and any maximal element is prime. Hence if every prime ideal of A is finitely generated then A is Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses generation of a+(x) by finitely many elements and examines (a:x) to reach contradiction if a maximal non-finitely generated ideal were reducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nilpotency in formal power series over Noetherian ring (Exercise 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A Noetherian and f = ∑_{n≥0} a_n x^n ∈ A[[x]], f is nilpotent iff each coefficient a_n is nilpotent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that nilradical N of A is nilpotent in Noetherian rings and that f∈N[[x]] implies f^m=0 for large m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of irreducible ideal being primary (Exercise 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a be irreducible ideal. The following are equivalent: (i) a is primary; (ii) for every multiplicatively closed S, (S^{-1}a)^c = (a:s) for some s∈S; (iii) for every x∈A the chain (a:x^n) is stationary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implications use standard localization properties and annihilator stabilization arguments; (i)⇒(ii) and (ii)⇒(iii) hold even without irreducibility, while (iii)⇒(i) uses proof of Lemma 7.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and closure properties of Noetherian rings (Exercise 7.4 variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Localizations of polynomial rings S^{-1}C[z] are Noetherian; certain rings of power series with positive radius form PIDs; other analytic-type rings may be non-Noetherian (examples given). Specific constructions show A=B + X^{k+1}B[X] is Noetherian when B is Noetherian, while other subrings of B[X,Y] can be non-Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various specific examples with hints: use Noether normalization, PID arguments, explicit ascending chain constructions (e.g., using sin(πz) example) or quotient-by-nilpotent-element arguments to show non-noetherianity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariant subring under finite group automorphisms is finite type (Exercise 7.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian, B a finitely generated A-algebra, and G a finite group of A-automorphisms of B, then the fixed ring B^G is a finitely generated A-algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the finite generation of B over A, Proposition 7.8 and Reynolds-operator-like averaging/polynomial relations arguments (exercise references provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely generated ring that is a field must be finite field (Exercise 7.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a finitely generated ring is a field K, then K is a finite field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: prime subring A is Z or F_p; Z impossible by finiteness arguments (Proposition 5.7); so prime field must be F_p and K finite extension ⇒ finite field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation of defining ideal for affine variety (Exercise 7.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affine algebraic variety X ⊂ k^n defined by possibly infinitely many equations f_α(t) = 0 is in fact defined by finitely many of them, i.e., the ideal they generate is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from k[t_1,...,t_n] being Noetherian: extract finite generating subset of the ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local property does not imply global Noetherianness (Exercise 7.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if each localization Ap (for all prime p) is Noetherian, A need not be Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to earlier exercises for counterexamples and to standard constructions where local rings are Noetherian yet global ring is not (see exercises 2.28 and 3.10ii references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibers of finite-type morphisms are Noetherian (Exercise 7.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f:A→B is of finite type, then for each p∈Spec(A) the fiber Spec(B⊗_A κ(p)) is a Noetherian subspace of Spec(B) (i.e., fibers are Noetherian).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: reduce to B quotient of A[x_1,...,x_n] and observe κ(p)⊗_A B is a quotient of κ(p)[x_1,...,x_n], which is Noetherian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert Nullstellensatz / radical-ideal equality (Exercise 7.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: For k algebraically closed and A=k[t_1,...,t_n], if V⊂k^n is variety defined by ideal a⊂A then I(V) = r(a) (the radical of a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard Nullstellensatz; reference to earlier paragraph where it's proven (6.2.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness/vanishing-Tor/free equivalences for finitely generated module over Noetherian local ring (Exercise 7.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (A,m,k) Noetherian local and M a finitely generated A-module. Then the following are equivalent: (i) M is free; (ii) M is flat; (iii) the map m⊗_A M → A⊗_A M is injective (i.e., m⊗M→M injective); (iv) Tor^A_i(k,M)=0 (for i=1? or vanishing of Tor as stated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classical local criterion relating flatness, freeness, Tor-vanishing and behavior mod m. See standard results (e.g. local flatness criteria) for details on which Tor-degree is required (usually Tor_1(k,M)=0).
